diagnostic_evidence.quote:
there exists a tower of
algorithms $\{\Gamma_{n_k,\ldots,n_1}\}$ such that 
$\Gamma_{n_k}(A) \uparrow \Xi(A)$ for all $A \in \Omega$.
Hence, we can compute the capacity of each output set $\Gamma_n^{\spec}(A)$ to obtain a $\Pi_1^A$ algorithm.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper defines Sigma_k and Pi_k via towers with monotone convergence, $\Gamma_{n_k}(A) \uparrow \Xi(A)$ and $\Gamma_{n_k}(A) \downarrow \Xi(A)$. The proof of Theorem thm_warm_up sets $\Gamma_n(A)=\widetilde{\Gamma}_n(A)-1/n$ where $\widetilde{\Gamma}_n$ approximates $f(\Gamma_n^{\spec}(A))$ to accuracy $1/n$ with two-sided error. This tower converges to $\Xi(A)$ with every term on the correct side (e.g., $\Gamma_n \le f(\Gamma_n^{\spec}(A)) \le \Xi(A)$ for a from-below limit), but it is not monotone: $\Gamma_{n+1}$ can drop below $\Gamma_n$, since the perturbations $\pm 1/n$ and the values $f(\Gamma_n^{\spec}(A))$ are not monotone. Likewise, the explicit towers in the examples compute $f(\Gamma_n^{\spec}(A))$ for the covers of \eqref{gamma_cover1}, and assumption (S1) only requires $\spec(A)\subset\Gamma_n^{\spec}(A)$ with each interval meeting $\spec(A)$; it does not assume the covers are nested, so $|\Gamma_n^{\spec}(A)|$, $\capacity(\Gamma_n^{\spec}(A))$ and the component counts $M_n(A)$ need not decrease/increase monotonically (the right-continuity $\capacity(K_n)\downarrow\capacity(K)$ invoked in ex:capacity applies only to nested $K_n\downarrow K$). Hence the constructed towers do not satisfy the paper's own definition of $\Sigma_1^A$/$\Pi_1^A$ (nor, via thm_warm_up2, the $\Sigma_2^A$/$\Pi_2^A$ claims under (S2)), so those memberships are claimed but not proved as written.

failure_location.quote: Let $\widetilde{\Gamma}_n(A)$ be an approximation of $f(\Gamma_n^{\spec}(A))$, computed to accuracy $1/n$ using $\Lambda$. We then set $\Gamma_n(A)=\widetilde{\Gamma}_n(A)-1/n$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace each claimed tower by its running extremum: for a Sigma-claim set $\Gamma_n := \max_{m\le n}\widetilde{\Gamma}_m$ and for a Pi-claim set $\Gamma_n := \min_{m\le n}\widetilde{\Gamma}_m$, using one-sided approximations of $f(\Gamma_m^{\spec}(A))$ (accurate from the required side) so each term stays on the correct side of $\Xi(A)$. Monotonicity then holds by construction, the limit is unchanged, and every stated classification (under (S1) and, with one extra limit, under (S2)) is recovered; no new lemma or weakening is needed.
issues.overall_effect: The one-sided convergence is proved, but the monotone (up/down) convergence required by the paper's definitions of Sigma_k/Pi_k is never established, so the advertised classifications ($\Sigma_1^A$ for connected components, $\Pi_1^A$ for Lebesgue measure and capacity, $\Pi_2^A$/$\Sigma_2^A$/$\Pi_3^A$ analogues under (S2), and the $\Sigma_3^A$ claims of fractal_dim_final obtained by the same argument) are unsupported by the given towers; the Delta-classification parts are unaffected.
issues.title: Constructed Sigma/Pi towers are not monotone, so the claimed Sigma/Pi classifications are not established
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short, local, routine modification of the displayed towers (running extrema with one-sided approximations); every substantive classification, rate, and guarantee of Theorem thm_warm_up, the examples, and the corollaries survives unchanged.
